1) deglycosylation enhances the antigenicity of HIV- 1 Env for both broad neutralizing antibodies and for their unmutated ancestor B cell receptors; 2) deglycosylating HIV-1 Env enhances immunogenicity of Env for the MPER epitope 2F5 in a macaque model.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a vaccine that can elicit neutralization of HIV-1 by antibodies that bind to the MPER region of gp41.
the development of improved HIV-1 Env immunogens that can induce broadly neutralizing antibodies and/or their reverted unmutanted ancestor (naive B cell receptor) antibodies.
the role of Env glycosylation on the immunogenicity and neutralization activity of HIV-1 Env.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
native deglyosylation of HIV-1 Env enhances the immunogenicity of gp41 MPER epitopes for both broad neutralizing mAbs as well as for their reverted unmutanted ancestor antibodies.

native deglycoylation of HIV-1 envelope gp140 enhances the antigenicity of the gp41 MPER region and thus, the immunogenicity of HIV-1 MPER epitopes for both broad neutralizing antibodies and reverted unmutated ancestral antibodies.
